title: Prenatal Followup
hpi: {{patient_name}} is a pregnant woman >20 weeks gestation with elevated BP (>140/90 on two occasions at least 4 hours apart) and no proteinuria and no end-organ damage. This is gestational hypertension (PIH) — distinguished from pre-eclampsia by absence of proteinuria and end-organ dysfunction. Risk factors: nulliparity, advanced maternal age, obesity, family history, multiple gestation. Must monitor closely for progression to pre-eclampsia (up to 25% progress). Management: if BP >160/110 → antihypertensive treatment (labetalol, nifedipine ER, methyldopa). If BP 140-159/90-109 → conservative monitoring, no medication needed but close surveillance. ACEI/ARBs CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy. Serial monitoring: BP checks, UA for protein, fetal growth US, NST/BPP starting at 32 weeks. Delivery at 37 weeks (no later than term). If develops pre-eclampsia features → manage as pre-eclampsia. Low-dose aspirin 81mg for pre-eclampsia prevention in high-risk women (started at 12-28 weeks).
